Here’s a concise review of your **Step 7** approach—no code changes.

## What you did

You set `images.remotePatterns` to a single entry built with `new URL('https://s3dbnt3uqdmuj4sr.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/**')` and dropped `placehold.co`.

## Is `new URL(...)` valid?

Yes for this stack. Next’s own types treat `remotePatterns` as `Array<URL | RemotePattern>`, and matching logic accepts both. So using `new URL(...)` is supported, not a hack.

## Blob host: specific ID vs `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com`

The guide called out the wildcard `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com`. You pinned **your** store host (`…public.blob.vercel-storage.com`).

That’s a solid choice:

- **Tighter allowlist** — only that store’s origin can be optimized by `next/image`, not every Vercel Blob tenant.
- **Trade-off** — if you ever point `ogImageUrl` at another Blob store (new project, new store, migration), you’d need another pattern or to switch to a wildcard/object form.

So: aligned with the intent (Blob + HTTPS), with a **stricter** hostname than the generic wildcard.

## Path `/**`

Using a URL whose path is effectively `/**` is the usual way to allow any object path on that host, which matches “any file in this Blob store.”

## Removing `placehold.co`

Reasonable **if** you no longer use `next/image` with `placehold.co` (e.g. local `/public` placeholder or non-`Image` fallback). A quick check: there’s no `placehold` reference in `grid-item.tsx` right now, so dropping the pattern is consistent. If any component still uses `placehold.co` with `<Image>`, you’d need that pattern back or change the placeholder source.

---

**Bottom line:** Your approach matches Step 7: HTTPS, Vercel Blob, and a single origin for optimized images. Using the concrete store hostname instead of `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com` is a deliberate, stricter variant of the same idea; `new URL` is fine per Next’s types. Just keep the placeholder story in mind if you reintroduce external placeholder URLs on `next/image`.

**Configuring env vars**

I can configure Vercel Blob URLs in environment variables for next.config.ts. I need to ensure env vars are properly configured for build-time access in next.config.ts. I can construct blob store URLs from env vars like `process.env.BLOB_HOSTNAME`. </details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2-fast)**_

Yes. `next.config.ts` runs in Node when Next loads the config (including `pnpm dev` and `pnpm build`), so you can read **build-time** env vars with `process.env`.

**How it fits your setup**

- Use a variable such as `VERCEL_BLOB_HOSTNAME` or `BLOB_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME` (the hostname only, e.g. `s3dbnt3uqdmuj4sr.public.blob.vercel-storage.com`), or a full base URL if you prefer to parse it.
- In `next.config.ts`, build `remotePatterns` from that value (e.g. `new URL(\`https://${process.env.VERCEL_BLOB_HOSTNAME}/**\`)` or the equivalent `RemotePattern` object with `protocol`, `hostname`, `pathname`).
- Define the value in `.env.local` locally and in the Vercel project **Environment Variables** for Preview/Production so every build gets it.

**You do not need `NEXT_PUBLIC_` for this** unless some **client** code also needs the same string. `remotePatterns` is only used by the Next/Image pipeline at build/runtime on the server side; the config file is not shipped to the browser as application code in the same way as `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` embeds. So a non-public name is fine and avoids exposing it in the client bundle unnecessarily (the blob URLs in your DB/HTML are already public anyway).

**Trade-offs**

- **Pros:** One place to change when the store/host changes; different values per environment; no store id committed in the repo if you care about that.
- **Cons:** If the var is missing, image optimization for that host can fail until you fix env—treat it like any required build config.

**Skills note:** This doesn’t conflict with App Router or RSC patterns; it’s static configuration. The image skill’s point about `remotePatterns` still applies: the optimizer must allow the host your `next/image` `src` uses, whether that host string is literal or from `process.env`.
